content.v: 近日Xbox首席执行官阿莎・夏尔马(Asha Sharma)在全员内部会议复盘公司现状。Xbox正经历行业罕见的大规模业务重组，近2000名员工受到裁员波及，夏尔马将危机很大一部分归因于过去过于激进的Game Pass订阅扩张路线。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261009/1791496889_446023_jpg_r.jpg
夏尔马坦言旧的Game Pass策略把Xbox的财务状况拖入“自由落体”，微软斥690亿美元完成动视暴雪收购，将《使命召唤》纳入订阅库之后矛盾进一步放大：一方面订阅运营成本疯狂暴涨，另一方面70美元定价的游戏本体销量被订阅模式挤压，业务两端同时承受损失。
订阅用户增长远不及内部预期：原本定下本年度7700万订阅用户目标，而实际Game Pass订阅规模仅约 3000 万，缺口巨大。过去押注订阅优先、多平台全面扩张的策略，没能兑现预想增长，还拉低Xbox整体利润率，显著低于行业同行，迫使团队启动全面业务重置。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261009/1791496889_445474_jpg_r.jpg
夏尔马也给出积极信号：经过裁员、调整业务架构之后，业务已经走出低谷。部分板块增长达到低谷时期的2‑3 倍，Game Pass结束连续八个月的用户下滑，订阅重回正向增长，留存数据得到改善。
但Game Pass未来走向依旧充满变数。市场传闻微软正在评估多项调整方案，包括上线带广告的低价订阅档位、修改第一方大作首发入库规则。目前官方尚未确认《上古卷轴6》、《光环》新作等重磅IP未来是否维持首日加入XGP，暂无确切答案。

items.title: Why a 21-year-old coder finally ported the real P.T. to PC: 'That something so influential could eventually become unplayable never sat right with me'
items.summary: Not emulation or a remake, a native PC port of Kojima's horror classic has arrived.

content.v: One of the most beloved horror games (demos?) of all time is finally free from the shackles of the PS4. Hideo Kojima's P.T. has been natively ported to PC by programmer Lorean Xavier, who made the project public this week. Not an emulator nor a remake, the native PC client does not contain any copyrighted materials—it requires a dumped copy of P.T. to function—but instead translates the original code into something that'll run on Windows and Linux.

That distinction not only sidesteps potential corporate scrutiny, but also allows Xavier to add modern graphical features and mod support to the PC version. It's an impressive effort that, according to the creator, has been in the works since 2024.

"I wanted to make the version of P.T. that my younger self always wished existed," Xavier, 21, told PC Gamer over email. "My attachment to the game goes all the way back to my childhood. I remember watching videos of it on my phone, wishing I could experience it myself. I didn't have a PS4, so playing the original was never really an option for me. I never imagined back then that I'd eventually be the one bringing it to PC."

The window to play P.T. "legitimately" was famously brief. Kojima surprise-dropped P.T. on the PlayStation Network in 2014 as a "playable teaser" for the Silent Hills reboot he was making with Guillermo Del Toro. When Kojima and Konami had a falling out, Silent Hills was canceled and P.T. got caught in the breakup, being delisted in early 2015. The horror classic has persisted only through emulation and preserved PS4 hard drives—until now.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/k4yRntF5mZN8zXCcRWucBj-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RPubjfA5Zo5vp4ZpXyQ9aj-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/weJsnK6JUUc4GmJdU4AqDi-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/EukeTD8C8yW9ZmkjZf6Xhi-1920-80.jpg
I think there's an important distinction between using AI as a development tool and blindly relying on it to create an entire project you don't understand.
Lorean Xavier, PT-PC developer
"The idea that something so influential could eventually become practically unplayable never sat right with me," Xavier added.

"There have been several PC remakes over the years, and I appreciate that people tried to preserve the experience, but none of them ever really satisfied me," Xavier said. "Something always felt off, whether it was the lighting, the atmosphere, the interactions, or the way certain events played out. They could resemble P.T. visually, but they never truly felt like the original to me.

"And that's exactly why I wanted to do this differently. I didn't want to make another interpretation of P.T. or recreate it approximately in another engine. I wanted the actual experience, with its original assets, sounds, animations, and behavior, running natively on PC."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/BGPbBNoqiTJTQBfQfatozh-1920-80.jpg
While the project is "not a modified version or fork of [PS4 emulator] shadPS4," the emulated version was an "extremely valuable" reference to compare the original game's behavior to the port.

We're in weird and wild times for the recompilation scene as gen AI has accelerated the creation of console-to-PC ports, often with janky, hastily-vibecoded results that make good preservation more difficult. Xavier is open about using AI in his workflow, but believes it's no replacement for "actually knowing what you're doing."

"I think there's an important distinction between using AI as a development tool and blindly relying on it to create an entire project you don't understand. In my case, I use AI to help with debugging, identifying issues, testing code, and working through problems when I get stuck. It can be incredibly useful for accelerating that process, especially when you're working alone on something this complicated.

"But I'm still the one responsible for the architecture, the implementation decisions, writing and reviewing the code, and understanding how the different systems fit together. My years of experience with reverse engineering and P.T. are what allow me to direct that process in the first place."

This is incredible. Unlike the previous decade of fan "recreations" of P.T. for PC which always seemed to miss important but minor details, this is (as far as I can tell?) a 1:1 port of the entire codebase. It creates all of the undocumented behavior I know of perfectly. October 7, 2026

In terms of faithfulness, the port has the seal of approval from at least one person who would know: Lance McDonald , the Australian creator who datamined P.T. and discovered many of its secrets back in the day, is impressed by what he reckons is a "1:1 port of the entire codebase."
You can check out the "PT-PC" project for yourself on GitHub.

content.v: 近日外媒IGN放出对R星North联席负责人罗布・尼尔森(Rob Nelson)采访，披露大量《GTA6》尚未公开的玩法细节。本作可能会加入更露骨的成人内容，包括性爱场景等。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261009/1791494050_791279_jpg_r.jpg
杰森与露西亚的浪漫亲密内容完全可选，不会强制玩家体验，也不提供战斗、收益类游戏加成，但会改变部分剧情演出走向。提升关系的方式不只有主线任务：双人可以打台球、迷你高尔夫、潜水、海滩漫步;一同抢劫作案同样能够增进感情。
角色之间会互相发送短信，长期无视消息会轻微降低好感;关系良好时可以触发牵手等互动。即便恋爱关系冷淡，二人依旧是犯罪搭档，主线剧情依旧可以正常推进。未操控的角色拥有独立日常行为逻辑，切换角色时，你可能撞见杰森正在洗澡等生活化场景。

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem Was Originally Planned as an Online Game, Producer Says
items.summary: Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/03/03/puzzle-site-1772543174828.png
Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online title before they scrapped the idea to focus on horror.

Kawata shared this information in the BIOHAZARD 30th Special Mook (‘magazine book’), a 124-page, full-color fan book with a complete history of the series' timeline, creature genealogy, and developer interviews.

“Every game is a continuous process of trial and error. For example, with Resident Evil Requiem, [game director Koshi Nakanishi] initially went so far as to develop it as an online game,” he said, via a fan translation.
“However, the results of research conducted partway through development were not favorable, so we decided to prioritize the horror concept once again and abandoned the online direction.”

That’s not the only wild thing Kawata revealed in the mook; he also said that Leon was the first character the team chose as a protagonist, but they ultimately felt that being able to hack and slash zombies with ease would lean too heavily on the ‘action’ side of things, making the overall game less scary.

“Leon was also the first character confirmed to appear as a protagonist. However, we determined that with Leon alone, who excels in combat, ‘horror would no longer work,’ so it was decided to introduce Grace as a new character,” he continued.

Kawata also explained why Capcom decided to wait before sharing Leon’s involvement in the game, saying, “by keeping the full picture of the game, which would develop along both the horror and action sides, until the very end, we were able to successfully maintain interest in it up until release.”

Nakanishi’s early plans to make RE9 an online game isn’t something totally surprising, given that management at Capcom had also pushed for Resident Evil 7 to have multiplayer and microtransactions during its conceptual phase.

"Right around that time, there was a big push at Capcom, a big 'marketing' push, saying 'we have to make the games players are asking for,'" franchise producer Jun Takeuchi said in 2022. "So we were being told 'make this, make that', it was really hard on the directors at the time. 'Online multiplayer' this, 'downloadable content' that. 'Ongoing service games! Microtransactions! Make a Resident Evil game that ticks all those boxes!'

“The idea of multiplayer got killed off pretty quickly. If we could properly put it together, we could make an exciting horror multiplayer game, but we didn’t really have any good ideas, so we set it aside. We went down the list, chopping them out, until we had marketing’s worst nightmare — a regular old single-player horror game."

Capcom is moving full speed ahead with many of its high-profile IPs, Resident Evil being one of them. The series just enjoyed a film adaptation directed by Zach Cregger, and a Code Veronica remake is set to release in February next year. Given that the devs of RE9 didn’t move forward with an online version of the game, it’s possible that we see another online Resident Evil title in the future — perhaps another Resident Evil Outbreak?

items.title: US government accuses Microsoft of replacing American workers with 'foreign indentured servants,' then gives Satya Nadella a medal
items.summary: The suspension of Microsoft's access to green card applications represents just another wildly incoherent day

content.v: Just three months after Microsoft shot down a racist conspiracy theory claiming the company was laying off thousands of American workers so it could replace them with foreigners via the H-1B visa program, the Trump administration has suspended the company's ability to apply for green cards for workers on the H-1B program, accusing it of fraudulently using the program to replace American workers with foreigners.
There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft
JD Vance, vice president of the United States of America

"The H-1B visa program is meant to allow companies to bring in the best of the best from outside the United States of America for positions that are completely impossible to fill with American workers," US vice president JD Vance said (via AP ). "Unfortunately, the program has become rife with fraud over the last several years—probably the last several decades.

"There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft ... Microsoft laid off last year 6,000 American workers. At the same time, the company benefitted from 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards. In other words, if you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one-and-a-half foreign indentured servants."

Calling H-1B visa holders "indentured servants" is certainly a choice, painting legal immigration as a form of human trafficking and the workers as victims, rather than specialists who've chosen to work in the United States.

Microsoft will still be able to hire non-American workers on a temporary basis via the H-1B program. It simply won't be able to apply to make them permanent, and thus grant them permanent residency, via the green card program—something that clearly does not comport with the Trump administration's intense focus on mass deportations .

"Our message to Microsoft and to any other foreign or domestic corporation is quite simple," Vance said. "We obviously want you to thrive in the United States of America. We want people to invest in the United States of America, but we want you to employ American workers.

"And so our message to Microsoft is you're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers. You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants."

Responding to Vance's message, Microsoft issued a statement saying it looks forward to "providing the administration with additional information," including that 80% of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it filed in the previous fiscal year "were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees," not to hire new employees. The remaining 20%, Microsoft said, were for new employees who were already in the country legally, rather than new arrivals.

Microsoft also addressed Vance's "indentured servants" comment directly, as well as claims that H-1B workers in general are paid significantly less than their American counterparts, saying it pays employees on H-1B visas "the same as any other employees doing comparable work."

Ironically, the suspension of Microsoft's ability to apply for permanent residency for H-1B visa holders comes on the same day that US president Donald Trump presented Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Other recipients honored today include X owner Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Dell Technologies chief Michael Dell, all of whom have been friendly with the Trump administration.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Gg5wUXbfsDJs8yAe5WBACf-1920-80.jpg

Trump recently disclosed significant Nvidia stock trades made in August, according to a new Reuters report. In September, the president renamed artificial intelligence to "Super Intelligence" and allowed the AI industry in the US to self-regulate .

items.title: Jason may or may not appear fully nude in GTA 6, but either way we've now seen his dong

others.title: No, I Have Not Seen Jason’s Penis in GTA 6

content.v: Cyberleek , the anonymous someone who's been sharing clips apparently taken from a Grand Theft Auto 6 development build, has returned after a hiatus with a new, 25-minute-long video that's circulating in places like the r/GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit and social media.

The most notable thing about the clip—or most noticeable , at least—is that protagonist Jason spends much of it naked. His genitals are fully modelled, physics and all, which isn't too surprising given we previously saw fully nude NPCs in another of Cyberleek's GTA 6 clips.

It remains unknown whether players will be able to walk around in the buff in the retail game, as Cyberleek presumably has access to developer tools. A floating tank seen partway through the clip makes it apparent that at least some console command shenanigans are at play. It's also notable that NPCs do not react to Jason's nakedness, and that the video shows first-person driving, a feature GTA 6 was previously reported not to include.

IGN did see a naked Jason during a cutscene in an official preview of GTA 6, but "thanks to some carefully positioned camera angles, his modesty remained entirely intact." So we just don't know, although it wouldn't be the first time a GTA game included full frontal male nudity of a prominent character, which occurred in GTA 4's The Lost and Damned DLC.

GTA 6 co-protagonist Lucia also appears topless in the Cyberleek clip, facing away from the camera and wearing a thong. Whether the underwear was the leaker's choice, or if GTA 6 unevenly enforces modesty, is also unknown.
A new era of videogame dong?

Whatever level of nudity GTA 6 ultimately does or doesn't allow—and once it's on PC, you can be sure that modders will make sure nothing is disallowed—it's a bit surreal to see how not-a-big-deal it all is after once experiencing Fox News hosts being scandalized by alien boobies in Mass Effect.

I want to say that things sure have changed since GTA's infamous Hot Coffee 'sex minigame' incident , but have they ? We're certainly far from a golden age of people being chill about things; you can't throw a stone on the internet without hitting some new sect shouting about its brand of traditional values (and the dietary supplements that complement it).

And yet it didn't seem like an especially big deal to conservative critics when Baldur's Gate 3 casually gave its characters detailed nude bodies and underwear lore. If it was, I didn't see it—perhaps it's just harder to stand out in today's noise bath of discourse.
Probably more relevant is that games just got more mainstream and have an older audience on average, and so they now have an easier time getting away with all the things Hollywood does.

As Andy observed recently after reaching out to infamous GTA critic Jack Thompson: "...Grand Theft Auto won. Netflix airs its special, the NBA wears its uniform, Walmart sells it, middle-aged cops and politicos buy it, and the state of Florida wraps itself in it."

Oh, and about Cyberleek: They're back to claiming they've got a "project" underway that you should help fund. I don't recommend that. Take-Two and Rockstar continue to look for the culprit, but we haven't heard any new developments on that recently.

items.title: Vampire games on Steam are a recession indicator and I have the charts to prove it
items.summary: Nothing is scarier during Halloween season than amateur statistics.

content.v: Despite what the GDP tells me, the economy in the real world doesn't feel like it's doing too hot for the average joe. But during the recent years' descent into compounding supply crises and mass layoffs affecting thousands of workers at once, I've noticed another trend: Sure does seem like there are a lot of vampire games in the mix lately.

I started to sense an uptick after Arkane's ill-fated Redfall in 2023. There was Vampire Survivors and V Rising—and Nighthawks, Moonlight Peaks, Blood of Dawnwalker, and more. Given current circumstances, you might think I'm just primed to notice nightmarish aristocrats bleeding us alive to sustain themselves. But after too many hours of spreadsheet data entry, I'm convinced devs really have been dabbling more heavily in Draculas as the economy feels increasingly dire. Vampire games on Steam are a recession indicator. And I have the charts to prove it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/FFY9R7fKJAew58Lp52P7y6-1920-80.jpg
Datawalker

At first glance, assessing whether Steam's vampire offerings can serve as a bellwether for economic sentiment could seem like a simple task. Steam has a Vampires tag, after all. The release dates are right there. Easy, right?
Wrong.

The Vampires tag is—perhaps fittingly—a horror. Devs and users freely slapping the label on anything with even one Dracula would be bad enough, but the advent of Vampire Survivors created a categorization disaster. Before Steam added a discrete bullet heaven genre, its countless imitators were content to use the Vampires tag as a makeshift discoverability solution. It's a mess in there.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CAvotnnQeZHhc2Pcwt5enA-1920-80.jpg

Not only that, but I wanted a more complete picture of Steam vampire activity than release dates alone can provide. When games on Steam might have taken anywhere from seven months to seven years to develop, it would've been fruitful to know when games were first listed to gauge the level of collective vampire interest among Steam devs.

Steam itself doesn't provide that info. SteamDB, however, tracks whenever a game first appeared during its scraping of Valve's store data. That's a good substitute for listing time—but unlike Steam proper, SteamDB doesn't have a public API for pulling that information.

End result: I individually sorted through the 1,213 Steam games with the Vampires tag at time of writing, manually collecting their release dates and first appearance in the SteamDB archive after determining whether they were, in fact, vampire-ass vampire games.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xB4qgQqpxLcq6tjTbNwWrT-1920-80.jpg
My process for parsing that last bit was pretty straightforward. A vampire game is a game whose developer sat down with an obvious interest in making a game about vampire stuff:

I'll admit there's an amount of subjectivity involved in my methodology, and it likely wasn't flawless—I only just realized that Resident Evil Village didn't appear in the Vampires pool, despite its big vampire lady being responsible for ongoing sexual awakenings for at least a third of the internet. But, if anything, my figures provide a conservative estimate: I excluded games that just didn't have that vampire stink on them despite literally starring Dracula as the protagonist.
Tragically, this means Hotel Transylvania 3: Monsters Overboard didn't make the cut. Apologies to Adam Sandler.
Unholy ascension

The results of my very professional data collection are clear: For years, the number of vampire games released on Steam has been increasing. In 2016, only four vampire games launched on the platform. A decade later, 65 vampire games have been released on Steam so far in 2026—and more have scheduled launch dates before the year's end.

There's been a sharp increase in the last six years. In 2020, the highest number of vampire games that launched in a single quarter was six; in 2026, it was 24. Developers are listing more vampire projects on Steam, too. Nine first appeared in SteamDB's archive in 2016; last year, 99 entered the database.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/W3qYUgXUU8JGWMNbSXhzxa-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/LPEKeyk7aj2or4DDmAKv8h-1920-80.jpg

It should be noted, of course, that the number of Steam releases in general has massively increased over the same period, from 9,634 game launches in 2020 to 21,263 in 2025. But it's not just the number of vampire games that's increased; it's the percentage.

The figure swings dramatically, but particularly over the last six years the percentage of vampire game launches has been trending steadily upwards, barring one particularly severe drop in mid-2025. The rate is still low—less than 1 in 100 games on Steam is a proper vampire game—but in some recent quarters, the percentage of vampire games was more than double what it was at the start of the decade.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pdgCJKRNaQ5nNJ7nXg6JmF-1920-80.jpg

I'd have liked to calculate similar percentages for how many vampire game listings have been popping up over the same period—but that would require manually recording the first SteamDB appearance dates for over 100,000 games. My bosses are already annoyed at the amount of time I've spent in spreadsheets this week.

Instead, I've calculated what I call the Vampire Menace Rating™ , which divides the number of quarterly vampire game appearances on SteamDB by the quarterly total of game launches on Steam to provide a more relative image of how vampires are occupying the total mindshare. While the resulting chart's trend line has a slight climb, I wasn't sure what to make of it at first glance… until I compared it to Dracula's Castle from Castlevania . The implications, I think you'll agree, are chilling:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rky8Q4ySEKKsVZxi34cLeU-1920-80.jpg
Okay, fine. The VMR™ might need some work. The increasing number and percentage of vampire games, however, is very real.
Blood forensics

Alright, so the number and percentage of vampire games on Steam has been trending upwards over the last six years. But can we really call that a recession indicator when we're still regularly hearing that the US stock market is breaking records and GDP is still embiggening? Sure, I might have a worsening sense of existential dread, but isn't everything good if the number is still going up?

If you happen to be—for example—one of those benefitting from the circular investments of infinite money into the emerging AI apparatus, you're probably delighted by the macroeconomic trends. But over those same six years, an accompanying set of signals indicate that, just as Nosferatus have skulked onto Steam, the average person in the US hasn't been thriving.

US Census Bureau data shows median household income rose between 2020 and 2025, even when adjusted for inflation—but only by about 4.6%. Costs, however, have risen faster. From the start of 2020 to now, the Consumer Price Index for all urban consumers—representing the costs of goods and services for roughly 88% of the US population—has increased by 27-29%, depending on whether you include the more volatile prices of food and energy.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gV6uGn2FCqoPncuVBAfqzh-1920-80.jpg

Likewise, the Producer Price Index for wholesale trade industries has climbed over the same timespan, meaning retailers are paying more for the goods they stock their shelves with—a cost increase that's passed onto the consumer.

Unsurprisingly, there are indicators that the average American is struggling with those increased costs. items.title: Ben Affleck Has Some Strong Opinions About Fortnite Skins And How Hard The Game Is For Him

content.v: Have you ever wondered what two-time Oscar-winner Ben Affleck thinks about Fortnite skins, and the game generally? You can now rest easy, as the man himself has weighed in with some strong takes.

Appearing on the New Heights podcast with brothers Jason and Travis Kelce, Affleck said he's a big gamer, and is particularly fond of first-person shooter games, so when he tried Fortnite, he thought he'd hold his own. That wasn't the case, though. He said not only did he get wiped out immediately, but the 12-year-olds he was playing against made fun of him after taking him out.
Affleck said he got heated and shouted back at the kids: "I don't suck! I'm a grown man!"

Affleck also told a brief story about how his son wanted Fortnite skins for Christmas, and he was shocked to learn the specific skins his son wanted cost hundreds of dollars. "They ain't even real? Just to wear in the game? That's bullsh**," Affleck said.
Affleck is a big fan of the competitive shooter Valorant . In the movie Gone Girl, Affleck's character can be seen playing Battlefield 3 .
Affleck is not the only person who has some strong words for the state of Fortnite. Writing for GameSpot, Phil Owen recently talked about why Fortnite sucks this season.

items.title: Ubisoft Shutting Down Rainbow Six Mobile After Less Than A Year
items.summary: Ubisoft has announced that Rainbow Six Mobile is shutting down, and it didn't have a very long life. The game

content.v: Ubisoft has announced that Rainbow Six Mobile is shutting down, and it didn't have a very long life. The game soft-launched in 2023, but properly rolled out for everyone back in February 2026. It will shut down on January 16, 2027, so it will have been online for less than a year in its full state for everyone.

"'We are proud of the passion, creativity, and dedication our team has put into the game," Ubisoft said. "One of the greatest parts of this adventure has been getting to experience it alongside you. We've loved seeing the memes, videos, strategies, tournaments, impossible plays, and all the countless moments that happened because you were here."

The developers are going to move on to "other long-term strategic projects," but Ubisoft did not say what these may be. The studio will share more details on the game's final days in the coming weeks.
"We are truly grateful to everyone who has played our game," the developers said.

Rainbow Six Mobile pitched itself as a mobile version of the extremely popular Rainbow Six Siege, which continues to crush it more than a decade after release. The next Rainbow Six game is Rainbow Six Tactics, and it's coming next year.

It's been a bumpy year for Ubisoft, as the company created a new organizational structure by way of its partnership with Tencent. As part of this, Ubisoft enacted mass layoffs, closed studios, and cancelled games .

items.title: Forza Horizon 6 Is Finally Coming to PS5 in January Alongside First Expansion

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/08/forzathumb-1791479830929.png
Forza Horizon 6 is finally coming to PS5 in January, and it will launch alongside a major expansion to the game.

A new trailer has confirmed that Forza Horizon 6 will race on to PS5 on January 26. It will arrive on the same day and date as the game's first major expansion, though no details have been revealed on what that will look like. As was the case with the Xbox and PC version of the game, players can pre-order the Premium Edition for extra goodies, including five days of early access to the game on PS5. Players who pre-order any version of the game on PS5 will also get a pre-tuned Ferrari J50.

The news of the game's release date comes after rumors that Forza Horizon 6 would miss its initial 2026 release window for PS5. The news confirms that to be the case, but it will launch just in time to remove itself from GTA 6's blast radius. This should ensure it performs well on PS5 and give the game a healthy audience. Forza Horizon 5 was a massive hit on PS5 when it was released on the console last year, so there is a strong demand for its sequel.
IGN gave Forza Horizon 6 a 10/10 in its review , praising it for it dense map, technical achievements, and well-paced campaign.

"I’ll always concede Forza Horizon 3 may forever be my favourite open-world racer, because who doesn’t love driving around their own backyard, but make no mistake: Forza Horizon 6 is unequivocally the best," reads an excerpt from our review. "The new standard in open-world racing is here, and it’s a gundamn masterpiece."

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Announces an NPC-ified Version of Shiva Voiced by Marisha Ray | NYCC 2026
items.summary: The Critical Role performer is also the real-life wife of the voice of Vincent Valentine.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/08/shiva-1791483258644.png

A seemingly new type of Shiva is joining Final Fantasy VII Revelation. At the game’s New York Comic Con panel, it was revealed that Critical Role performer Marisha Ray is joining Revelation as “Polydroid Shiva.” It wasn’t explained how, exactly, this pointy version of the series-recurring ice lady summon will fit into Revelation, but in the BTS clip played during the panel, she seemed to be announcing a snowboarding minigame and blamed Vincent for her “situation.”

“Have you any of the faintest idea of the consternation you’ve caused?” Polydroid Shivia says. “Polydroid problems aren’t my purview,” Vincent replies. (Cold, brother!) She then demands him to, “Drop on a board, caped one, and give my slopes a spin. Let us see how you carve!”

Ray stood up from the front row of the panel, but did not join the stage. Moderator Lucy James asked Matt Mercer, the voice of Vincent Valentine and Ray’s real-life husband and Critical Role co-star, what it was like acting alongside Ray and seeing her in the game. “It was amazing, are you kidding me!” Mercer said. “[Shiva] is her favorite summon in the whole series.”

When they realized they were sharing scenes together after Ray was booked, he said they celebrated, but had one hesitation. “Talking to the team, too, it was like, ‘I hope this wasn’t any nepotism scenario,’” Mercer said. “It was like, ‘Oh no, they didn’t know she was your wife.’ I was like, ‘That’s right, you earned that, baby!’”

The hour-long panel was a sendoff for the cast, many of whom have spent nearly seven years recording for these roles. Cody Christian, who voices Cloud, estimated he’d spent “800 hours collectively” in the booth to nail his lines. “Every inflection, every breath, it all matters. We’d spend 10 minutes on 3 wo r ds just to make sure it was right,” he said.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation releases on April 8, 2027. Director Naoki Hamaguchi (who was not at the NYCC panel, but thanked fans via prerecorded video message) has said that the game will take more than 100 hours for completionists to beat .

items.title: A Live-Action Cyberpunk 2077 Movie Is in the Works at Paramount
items.summary: Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film.

content.v: Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film.

Deadline has reported that the film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, who is best known for producing the Transformers and GI Joe films. CD Projekt Red is also onboard to produce, though there is no word on any actors, writers, or directors attached to the project. It's unclear if it will faithfully adapt the titular video game from 2020, or if this will be another story set in the Cyberpunk universe, similar to Netflix's animated Edgerunners series.
On X, CDPR co-CEO Michał Nowakowski expressed excitement about Cyberpunk's upcoming film adaptation.
"We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise," he said. "We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time."

If this is a straight up adaptation, Paramount already has some built-in starpower that it can utilize. In the game, Keanu Reeves played Johnny Silverhand, a radical Tyler Durden-style character that lives in the protagonist's head. Idris Elba also joined the game's cast in an expansion known as Phantom Liberty, which feels like a really cool storyline to adapt, though it may not work as well as a mainstream entry point into that universe. Either way, it's exciting to hear that Night City is making its way to the big screen.

CD Projekt Red is also hard at work on the next Cyberpunk game , which is expected to release after The Witcher 4. As a result, we may not see the next game until 2029 or 2030 at the absolute earliest. But that may also be perfect timing, as a Cyberpunk film may not be ready until around that time either. Reeves has already expressed interest in appearing in the next Cyberpunk game , so maybe he'd play Johnny Silverhand on the big screen too.

Paramount is leaning heavy into major video game adaptations, as it has Street Fighter releasing next weekend. In 2028, the studio will also release a Call of Duty movie written by Taylor Sheridan and directed by Peter Berg. Paramount is making all kinds of big moves, as it just merged with Warner Brothers , meaning it has a wealth of new IP to take advantage of.

items.title: A great indie studio is making a sequel to one of my favorite adventures 17 years later, for one simple reason: 'We're not getting any younger, and the world seems to be ending'
items.summary: Machinarium 2 is finally happening.

content.v: I just made a noise like air being slowly released from a balloon .

It's been 17 years since the original Machinarium , a wordless tale of love in a crumbling city of robots. Amanita Design has put out some great games over that span— Botanicula , Chuchel , Creaks , Phonopolis —but hasn't breathed even a hint that more Machinarium might be on the way. So why now?

"We're not getting any younger, and the world seems to be ending, so if we were ever going to make Machinarium 2, now is the right time," Amanita CEO and designer Jakub Dvorský said—a bit dark, sure, but I can't find any factual fault in his reasoning. "We're also grateful to every player who waited patiently all these years. We couldn't have done it without them."

The new game picks up where Machinarium left off: Having escaped the city, Josef and Berta crash-land in a hidden valley populated by two robot tribes, one in the Elektrona monastery and the other in the city of Oilton—both of them facing a grim future as their power is slowly running out. While Machinarium 2 promises the same style of point-and-click puzzling as the original, Josef and Berta are both playable this time around, swappable at will, and will have to work together to solve the game's puzzles.

The distinctive visual style of Machinarium is back—perhaps a little sharper than the first game, although I think it still looks great—and importantly, so is Tomáš Dvořák, aka Floex, the composer whose soundtrack helped make Machinarium so distinctive and memorable.

As PC Gamer's Evan Lahti explained some years ago, music is one of the best parts of Amanita games , and Dvořák is responsible for much of it. Given his many years of collaborating with the studio on most of its games, it's not really surprising that he's back for Machinarium 2, but it is reassuring to have it confirmed.

"When I composed the first Machinarium soundtrack years ago, I never anticipated such a huge response," Dvořák told me. "I was simply trying to have fun and enjoy the creative process—and I believe that is the exact same approach I need for the sequel.

"Naturally, it’s a challenging task. It is easy to fall into the trap of comparing my new work to the original, and doubts occasionally creep in about whether it will be as engaging. However, I try to minimize those thoughts. Experience has taught me that the best way to create is to simply 'have fun'."

Interestingly, Dvořák said he didn't really think about Machinarium 2 as a sequel at all: Instead, it's more "a beautiful project [that] provides a great opportunity to create a specific kind of music ... the visuals have an incredible influence on the music universe I create. Machinarium is exactly the kind of environment where things grow very naturally for me."

The music in the Machinarium 2 trailer certainly has a familiar vibe, but Dvořák said he set a few specific goals for himself to differentiate it from the original: The soundtrack to be "more melodic and musical," something he aims to achieve with "more simplicity, which is actually the hardest part: Usually, unique organic details come from layering many sounds together."
And of course, the passage of time is a factor too: "I feel the new music is more mature," Dvořák said, "simply because I am older."
Aren't we all? Still great music, though.

As for the real reason Amanita Design opted to go back to Machinarium now, all these years later, it really was just a vibe situation. "I tend to make these kinds of decisions more intuitively than rationally. That’s just how I work," Dvorský, Amanita's CEO, told me in a separate chat.

"I guess I rely on some kind of instinct or feeling, so it’s actually quite hard for me to give you a clear, logical answer. I just had this feeling that the world of the robots was knocking on the door, asking to come out again. It seemed like a good idea, and little by little, I got really excited about it."

It's probably self-evident at this point, but I'm really excited about it too. Machinarium was Amanita Design's first full-length, standalone game, and it made me an immediate fan of the studio. Amanita's subsequent games have more than lived up to the high standard it set, but even so there's always been a very faint 'wish it was Machinarium' hanging in the background over every new release. Well, here we are—I guess now I can start quietly pining for Botanicula 2.

Machinarium 2 doesn't have a release date at this point, but it's up for wishlisting on Steam and GOG . For now, you can pick up Amanita's previous releases —including the original Machinarium—at some pretty sweet prices until October 15.

content.v: It took a while but there's finally an official way to hunt and kill some of Subnautica 2's most annoying sea creatures. The only catch is, you'll have to do it in Dave the Diver DLC—though as catches go, that's a pretty fun one.

The crossover was announced today at the Triple-I Initiative showcase. Coming in early 2027, the Dave the Diver X Subnautica 2 content pack will suck Dave into the alien waters of Unknown Worlds' survival game where he can mine resources, hunt fish, and—one would hope—discover some tasty new sushi recipes for Bancho to cook up. Here's the trailer:

What caught my eye even more than the glimpse of a massive and intimidating boss at the end of the trailer were those pesky Nibbler Mangos, which start biting you the second you dive into Subnautica 2 and never really stop. Players having no way to kill large enemies in Subnautica 2 has been a bit of a controversy , with some even resorting to mods so they can fight back.
It's nice that players can finally get a bit of revenge against those relentless fish, albeit in another game.

"We're thrilled to see Subnautica 2's creatures, including the Nibbler Mango, join Dave's world," Mintrocket told PC Gamer via email. "The team had a lot of fun bringing these creatures into our game, and players can expect the DLC to play just like the Dave the Diver they know and love."
As for those saddened to hear this is the final DLC for Dave the Diver, that doesn't necessarily mean it's the definitive end of his adventures.

"While this will be the final major DLC for Dave the Diver, there may still be smaller content updates or collaborations based on player feedback and our internal plans," Mintrocket told PC Gamer. "Since we're not moving straight into a sequel, we'll keep thinking about ways to make sure players don't forget Dave and his friends." Bancho the Chef, meanwhile, is getting his own game , a prequel, though a release date has yet to be announced.

content.v: Ahead of GTA 6 's release in November, Rockstar Games has announced an official merch collection for the game, and it includes some snazzy stuff like a t-shirt featuring an alligator wearing sunglasses and drinking a cocktail.

Of note, Rockstar says its t-shirts should be machine washed cold, but not put in the dryer. Instead, you should hang them on a line, Rockstar says.

items.title: Strange Scaffold Saved This New Tactics Game From Cancellation
items.summary: One of the more interesting game reveals from today's Triple-i Initiative showcase was Gods With Badges, a nar

content.v: One of the more interesting game reveals from today's Triple-i Initiative showcase was Gods With Badges, a narrative-driven tactics game about a disgraced police officer returning to the line of duty. What makes Gods With Badges even more fascinating is that it was canceled by its original developer and saved by El Paso, Elsewhere developer Strange Scaffold.

The press release announcing Gods With Badges explained that the project began at Artificer, the Devolver Digital-owned studio behind games like Minos, Sumerian Six, and Showgunners . Originally called Hard Justice, the project ultimately didn't pan out and almost never saw the light of day.

Meanwhile, Strange Scaffold is spearheading an initative called Project Share, which encourages developers to share the original code for their games so other studios can riff on it. This previously helped enable the development of another Creepy Redneck Dinosaur Mansion game and has now saved an Artificer game from cancellation.

The press release explains that Gods with Badges took the work already completed by Artificer and reinterpreted it "through Strange Scaffold's distinctive creative lens." Studio Head Xalavier Nelson Jr. added that he is "deeply grateful to the original developers at Artificer for trusting us with their project, and can't wait for people to see what we've built on this complex, exciting foundation."

Gods With Badges follows a disgraced police officer named Harrow McClellan as she patrols the dystopian city of Scarhelm. Each encounter starts with choice-driven conversations but can devolve into isometric, turn-based combat. Players can even turn off their bodycam to gain access to more combat abilities, though this will obviously affect how the narrative plays out.
I expect this game to tackle subjects like police brutality and the role of law enforcement in an increasingly dystopian world. Gods With Badges will be released on PC sometime in 2027.

items.title: I have added roving bands of militant furries to Grand Theft Auto 5
items.summary: Thereby bringing it a bit closer to real life.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

Let's get one thing out of the way: I think we, as a society, as a people, are generally fine with furries at this point. The phenomenon of ragging on furry subculture has been, gladly, consigned to the dustbin of history. It's a 2010 disease from which we have convalesced. Let nothing I write from here on be taken as a slight against them.
That being said, it is very funny to give someone in a fursuit a gun and a military objective.

I have installed, well, two mods actually. The first, preliminary mod is Gang and Turf Mod , which adds a sort of gang war system in the vein of GTA: San Andreas. Different factions will wage war over areas of Los Santos, from the heart of downtown up to the podunk rural hamlets in the north.

Then I installed the main course: Furry Gang for Gang and Turf Mod , which festoons the city streets with murderers in wolf outfits who are here to take their corners with blood and gunpowder. There are other gangs—gangs installed by default with the base mod—but I honestly didn't pay much attention to them. Some of them were in suits? They truly all got steamrolled by the marauding bands of fursuited raiders.

Like an embedded reporter in a war, I followed one band of armed furries into battle. Dodging cars, they dispatched most of their foes pretty quickly, but then a tornado manifested and started whipping them into the sky. At one point, I punched one of them, mostly out of overstimulation. Then I got eaten by the tornado too. Then I teleported somewhere else. Nearby, on a ridge, was a single furry in a purple suit, immobile and gazing, planning some future conquest.

items.title: 35% of Marvel's Wolverine Sales Were on Disc, According to Analyst Data
items.summary: According to retail data, 35% of Marvel’s Wolverine sales were physical discs.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/13/wolverine-again-1786621307864.jpg
According to retail data, 35% of Marvel’s Wolverine sales were physical discs. This comes from Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business ), which tracks sales data across major markets globally.

The data suggests Wolverine shifted 2.16 million units in September (it went on sale September 15), and a significant portion of those sales were on-disc. In Europe, 51% of Wolverine sales came from the boxed version. Zooming in, more than two thirds were physical sales in France, but two thirds were digital in the UK.

The data comes in the wake of Sony's controversial announcement that it will phase out physical disc production for PlayStation by 2028, which sparked an online backlash and calls for a U-turn from some organizations who campaign for physical media.

“If platform owners are deciding to eliminate physical media and older digital storefronts, then we'd also like to see trade groups like the Entertainment Software Association offer meaningful solutions for archives and museums to legally preserve digital-only content and make it accessible for research,” the Video Game History Foundation has said.

Earlier this month, former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden questioned Sony's decision to kill discs , saying: "I do think, particularly in the gaming realm, maybe 80% of the people download and 20% don't, whatever that breakdown might be, but that's a super important 20%. I mean, that is largely the most faithful of the faithful, that is, many times, the people who buy two copies of every game, one never gets out of the shrink wrap, and you play the other one."

However, there is no indication that Sony will change its mind on this. In July, Sony acknowledged “strong views” from the video game community on the issue, but insisted it wouldn't budge . Elsewhere, the biggest game of the year has no physical version. There are no plans at all for a disc version of GTA 6 , and even the special edition contains a code in an otherwise empty box.

Insomniac’s brutal superhero game was the second best-seller on PS5 last month, beaten only by EA Sports FC 27. EA’s soccer game sold close to 5 million copies on PS5 and 1.65 million on Xbox, reflecting the difference in install base between the two consoles.

How to Fish and Wardogs both outperformed Wolverine when factoring in PC as a platform. Wardogs closed in on 3 million sales, carried by strong word of mouth and viral social media clips of its combat sandbox. Only EA Sports FC 27 on PS5 outsold the Bulkhead and Team 17 shooter in September.

Many other titles were off to a much slower start in September. Ampere’s data shows 305,000 sales on PS5 for Control: Resonant and 291,000 for Silent Hill: Townfall . The Blood of Dawnwalker , the debut RPG from a team of former The Witcher developers at Rebel Wolves, fared much better, boasting 1.8 million sales across all platforms.

items.title: Arc Raiders’ Big Update Has It Surging To Numbers It Hasn’t Seen In Months
items.summary: When Embark said it would take several months to deliver the major Arc Raiders update it envisioned, days like

content.v: When Embark said it would take several months to deliver the major Arc Raiders update it envisioned, days like today were probably the goal. The extraction shooter is once again high up in Steam's charts for both best-selling and most-played games.

Among best sellers, Arc Raiders currently ranks fifth, behind this week's other big releases, Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Gears of War: E-Day, but those came out earlier this week, and it's still early, so we may see it leap over those before the week is through. Its new cosmetic DLC, the Frozen Trail Collector's Set, is also selling very well. It currently sits at #8 on the best-sellers list.

As for concurrent players, Arc Raiders has eclipsed triple digits on Steam, something it hasn't done since May. It's sitting at 106,000--that's good for 12th on the list--and has actually gained 5,000 more players since I started writing this. Like its sales surge, it seems likely that it'll keep climbing throughout the day.

Not coincidentally, May was when Embark announced it would be moving to a semi-annual cadence for major updates , with today's Frozen Trail being the first such update since that change. Embark felt it needed more time to deliver bigger updates for players while giving developers breathing room for a healthier work environment.

I've been fascinated by that bold move because it's rarely seen in the world of extremely popular live-service games. Arc Raiders never really dropped off completely; it still averaged 40,000 concurrent Steam players in September, but it was close to averaging half a million last holiday season, so the fall was precipitous, even if those numbers were likely never to be sustained.
The first day post-update can't tell the whole story on whether this revised roadmap pays off for Embark, but it's clearly off to a strong start.
Arc Raiders will be free-to-play this weekend on all of its available platforms.

items.title: Triple-I Initiative October 2026: Everything Announced At The Showcase
items.summary: We normally get only one Triple-I Initiative showcase per year, but 2026 is proving to be the exception. The s

others.title: ‘Enough Games Have Been Cancelled and Shut Down. That Betrayal Has Ramifications’ – Is It the Beginning of the End for Live-Service Games?

content.v: We normally get only one Triple-I Initiative showcase per year, but 2026 is proving to be the exception. The second broadcast of the year from organizers Evil Empire, the Triple-I Initiative was a focused blast of curated trailers and game updates, all rolling out across an almost-hour-long livestream. If you don't have time, fret not, because we've recapped everything below for you to check out. Most of these games also have demos that are now live on Steam, so if you like what you see, you can get an early taste of them right now.
Aftergods

After Ragnarok annihilated most of the deities who safeguarded the land, it's up to the survivors of that cataclysm to form a new pantheon and push back the monsters that have risen up in their absence. The debut trailer for Aftergods featured some godly DNA--it was produced by the team behind the Blood of Zeus and Castlevania animated series--and this top-down survivalite ARPG is coming to PC, Xbox Series X|S, and PS5.
Waltz and Jam

Korean developer Flyway Games announced hand-drawn action-adventure Waltz and Jam has a release date, and you can get your hands on this cute little afterlife game starting December 3. It'll be launching for PC, Switch 2, and PS5.
Among Us Story: On Guard

A new Among Us standalone game in which you have to prove your innocence before the Impostor gets to the rest of the crew? Nothing sus about that! Billed as both a narrative and detective game, Among Us Story: On Guard launches on February 17, 2027 for PC, Switch consoles, and mobile.
Astral Ascent

Astral Ascent's next update adds some Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 flavor to the popular roguelite, as well as a ton of new content. The free Expedition 33 For Those Who Come After update is now available on PC and console, adding new summons, bosses, and a huggable Esquie. Wheeeee!
Brotato: Primal Dread
The Primal Dread DLC for Brotato is out on November 2 for PC, adding bigger enemies, new brotatoes, and weaponized panflutes.
Canyons

A new co-op PvE shooter from the creators of Breathedge, Canyons drops you into a brutal, ever-changing world populated with supernatural creatures known as the Awakened. Everything from tombstones to thrones is out to harm you in this strange world, but an itchy trigger finger and Blood Pacts that allow you to wield exotic abilities will help keep you alive long enough to establish a settlement. Canyons is coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S in November 2027.
Chained Together

Co-op game Chained Together is getting its first new map on November 12. Your climb out of hell is just getting started, and a new gameplay mode will also test teams by seeing just how quickly they can overcome the trials of the damned.
Dandelion Void

Dandelion Void has a simple premise: The game wants to know if you have what it takes to survive the hostile jungle-choked halls of a derelict spaceship adrift between the stars. You'll need to establish a refuge to keep the horrors at bay, and if that sounds like a grand time, you can try a demo ahead of its Steam Early Access launch next year.
Dave the Diver X Subnautica 2 DLC

After teaming up with Sega's Yakuza series and running into Godzilla, Dave the Diver's next crossover brings the wet world of Subnautica to his shores. Out in early 2027, you can expect the casual single-player adventures of Dave the Diver to be fused with the alien oceans of Subnautica 2--which should make for some interesting sushi dishes.
Drunken Goddess Reflux

Summary: From the developers of "Yunyun Syndrome!? Rhythm Psychosis" comes their latest title: Drunken Goddess Reflux! Play shot-glass Russian roulette against Femme Soule, a demon who loves you to death--literally! Break the rules as you drink in this twisted game of Russian roulette, and push the demon until she spills it all.
Escape The Backrooms

And now for some liminal horror! Escape the Backrooms is getting a new "After Party" update in December, adding new levels to the game. New skins are also coming later this month, and if you haven't tried it yet, Escape the Backrooms is a co-op game that builds on the idea of analog horror. It's available for PC and consoles.
False Echo

Like Papers, Please combined with Das Boot, False Echo's blend of submarine warfare and cryptography thrills will be surfacing on PC in Spring 2027. To give you an idea of what the full game will be like, you can try the demo right now.
Gods with Badges

Fans of turn-based tactics games have been eating well lately, and Gods with Badges from Strange Scaffold (I Am Your Beast, Space Warlord Baby Trading Simulator) looks like another delicious entry in that genre. With a focus on narrative sequences and brutal turn-based battles, players will step into the boots of disgraced police officer Harrow McClellan as she seeks to change lives and pursue her own version of justice. Combat requires you to follow the rules, but turning off your body-cam can unlock special dialogue and combat options if you're prepared to deal with the consequences of going dark.
Haunted Paws

A spooky co-op game where you get to play as two adorable dogs? Sign us up! Haunted Paws lets you send your puppies on an adventure through a haunted mansion to locate your missing owner, and it's coming to PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and Switch. On PC, you can grab a demo for it on Steam.
Hela: of Mice & Magic

Out on December 1, Hela: Of Mice & Magic is a cute adventure game featuring a brave little mouse. Set in a world inspired by Northern Sweden, the game encourages you to be a force for good. A PC demo is out now, and the game launches on December 1 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Switch 2, and Switch. It'll also be a day-one release through Xbox Game Pass.
Risk of Rain 2: Hallowed Concepts
The Escapists 3
Team17 revealed a new entry in The Escapists franchise, building on the foundation of previous games to offer more 3D prison hijinks. It's out in 2027.
Machinarium 2

Amanita Design has a new Machinarium sequel on the way, almost 20 years after the first game was released. There's no release date yet, but so far it looks like a gorgeous follow-up to the original, with its unique art.
Lazare's Sacrifice

A narrative deckbuilder that has been designed in collaboration with Damien Monnier--the game designer behind the original Gwent and Gwent: The Witcher Card Game--Lazare's Sacrifice is set during the height of the French Revolution, and it tasks you with not losing your head.
The Talos Principle 3
The final entry in the series, The Talos Principle 3 is once again being developed by Croteam, and it'll offer plenty of thought-provoking puzzles to solve.
Militsioner

First revealed in 2020, Militsioner is an immersive talking sim with a unique hook--you're being followed by a Godzilla-sized policeman, who is keeping a giant eye on you in spite of your protestations of innocence. You need to pack your bags and skip town to avoid the extremely long arm of the law, but be careful, because the Giant Policeman is watching your every move.
Pony Island 2
The next game from Inscryption creator Daniel Mullins, Pony Island 2 is getting a public playtest soon.

items.title: Amazon is roasting users with their own shopping habits, but it don't have nothin' on us
items.summary: Getting to know you, getting to know all about you…

content.v: If you've got an Amazon account, then you likely already realise Steve Bezos' corporate empire is hoovering up your data so it can better sell to you. What's surprising is when Amazon actually offers a peek behind that vast curtain of data, revealing what it's learnt about you and potentially reading you for filth in the process.

Amazon's 'About You' feature rolled out back in May. It gained more attention this week after one Threads user's viral post appeared to show that, based on her 'Product Preferences,' Amazon thought she had "flat buttocks." They weren't the only ones left "literally speechless," as another user shared that Amazon had noted they do " not trust people easily ." A Reddit user posted that Amazon had noted they apparently get " a tired gray cast from lack of sleep ".

Obviously, I had to take a look at whatever strays I was catching from the About You feature myself. Alas, my About You is frightfully boring and served only to remind my lactose-intolerant self that I prefer 'plant-based milk' and that I 'systematically [replace] consumable household items' like my preferred brand of milk that doesn't make my tummy hurt. So, I opened up the question to the wider PC Gamer team.

items.title: As it lays off developers and closes studios, Xbox gets into the movie business
items.summary: Asha Sharma's latest big move is all about bringing "franchises" to the world in ways that don't involve games

content.v: More big news out of Xbox today: A new division called Xbox XP will take the lead on "film and television, consumer products, strategic partnerships, and live experiences," with a focus "on how people experience our franchises beyond the games themselves."
As detailed on today's announcement , here's what that breaks down to:

Xbox XP will be headed by Kayleen Walters, who previously spent a couple years as president of Minecraft studio Mojang and before that spent close to a decade in different brand and "franchise development" roles at Microsoft. Prior to that she spent 13 years at Lucasfilm, finishing her time there as vice president of franchise marketing and integrated planning.

"XP is a play on 'experience points'," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma helpfully explained in a separate internal email , "and formalizes four investment areas for us: Xbox Pictures for film and television adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences.

"Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Gad5tyvebe3wMApBPfPum-1920-80.png

Well, what to make of this, eh? It sounds ambitious, superficially at least, although what it adds up to in practice remains to be seen: It's possible that Xbox XP represents more of a reshuffling of pre-existing departments and efforts already in the works, with a new executive atop the org chart to put some extra punch in the announcement.

But it comes while Xbox is in the midst of laying off thousands of people who make the actual games that serve as the foundation of these franchises. Make of that what you will, but for myself, kicking off a whole new (and very expensive-sounding) Xbox division while Ninja Theory is bleeding out on the floor is not a great look. It also stands in rather sharp contrast to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella called the "streamlining" of Xbox . This is streamlining?

A Minecraft Movie was a massive hit and I have no doubt the sequel will be too, and it's understandable that Microsoft would want a bigger piece of that action. But how many other franchises really share that space? Is anyone particularly jazzed for the Modern Warfare movie in development, or disappointed that the Halo TV series ( Master Chief had sex ) was cancelled? WoW nostalgia is running hot these days, but hot enough to draw people to theaters or drive subscriptions to Prime? I don't see it.

Movies and TV are the big eye-catcher here, but the other three "investment areas"—products, partnerships, and places—are potentially more impactful on the actual videogame front. I'm particularly struck by the image of BlizzCon in the Xbox XP announcement: BlizzCon is easily the most studio-centric major gaming convention in existence (it's literally the Blizzard Convention ), but it's not too hard to imagine a branding shift there—'Xbox BlizzCon,' maybe—and an expansion into non-Blizzard games. Blizzard is Activision, after all, and Activision is Xbox. What sort of immediate practical impact that would have on the games we play or events we attend is debatable, but the loss of studio culture is a loss for gaming culture.

There's a lot of wait-and-see here, in other words, but those of you with long memories may know that this isn't Xbox's first attempt to bust into the glitzy world of showbiz: In 2012, it launched Xbox Entertainment Studios , a film and television production company intended to develop "interactive TV" content for the Xbox 360. It was shuttered in 2014.

items.title: All hail the long steam machine, Pimax's new SteamOS-ready mini PC
items.summary: It looks like a Steam Machine, and it runs SteamOS, so it must be a steam machine.

content.v: You could say Pimax is copying Valve's homework with its new mini PC, the Spation. Though the Steam Machine is merely a black box, so you could say it also copied any number of other miscellaneous black rectangles itself; the Xbox Series X among them. Nevertheless, this is one similar-looking living room machine, and Pimax is even pitching it with SteamOS.
Pimax's machine is a mini PC with a whole bunch of power behind it. Pimax says it comes with either an RX 9070 XT or RTX 5070 Ti , and a Ryzen 7 9800X3D .
It packs in 32 GB of DDR5, a 1 TB SSD, and a 1000 W SFX PSU. It also supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, and comes with 2x DisplayPort 2.1, 1x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB4, and 6x USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports.
So, it's much more capable than Valve's li'l box, though I shudder at the thought of the price. Pimax has not yet announced a price or launch date.
You can see how it all slots together under the removable rear panel in the render provided by Pimax below.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KmcRQKqPE47saZUBgsyr9N-1920-80.png

Most of the I/O is accessible at the back of the device. Slightly above and behind that is what looks to be a Mini-ITX motherboard with two DIMMs installed, presumably with some sort of solution to shift the rear I/O. Above that, the power supply, with a fan mounted above it. The GPU sits flat on the reverse of the unit, using a PCIe riser cable.

My only concern is how well that graphics card can breathe in there, and more broadly for temps, but there may be yet more fans within the unit. The front panel looks to be removeable—just like the Steam Machine—with some venting in there for the GPU.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3PVrcdQwfjjKcCqGPkdJ3N-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wZs3KQEveRAKDxgRZt3m6N-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MZ245tXb6JDdX2Jx2xuw6N-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/UCY6recWAhPsmRDYGtF9KN-1920-80.png

It looks like a pretty smart layout, and not totally dissimilar to a Fractal Terra —the case I use for my own mini PC—sat upright. Pimax plans to offer a barebones kit that will require a user to install their own GPU, storage, and memory, which means at least parts of it are set to be pretty standardised.

The idea behind the Spation is to be more powerful than a gaming laptop to power high-end PC VR, in a smaller size than your average PC. Thereby easier to shift besides your TV unit for a spot of virtual reality in the evening. There is a bit of a gap in the market for this sorta thing—beyond simply building your own Mini-ITX gaming PC—as the real Steam Machine has been known to struggle with VR due to its Arch-based SteamOS.

Though that might also be the case for the Spation. Pimax is pitching it with both Windows and SteamOS support. It is just a regular PC, after all, so there's nothing stopping you from loading SteamOS onto anything with compatible hardware—namely AMD's gear, as Nvidia GPU support is an ongoing process in SteamOS. Which you choose should probably depend on whether you are planning to use it for VR or not. Even though the Steam Frame has shown what Linux can do in VR, and Pimax says it's bringing Pimax Play to Linux as a dedicated client, it does feel like Windows remains the easiest option.
